name: H-box identity
summary: Two arity-2 H-boxes in a row are the identity, up to a factor of 2.
description:
An arity-2 H-box with the standard label $-1$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, i.e. $\sqrt 2$ times a Hadamard gate. Two of them in a row therefore give twice the identity. This is the ZH counterpart of [Hadamard cancellation](../hadamard-cancellation/).

In the completeness paper of 2021 it is shown that this rule is actually derivable from the other rules of the phase-free ZH-calculus.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
